page_title: Bitcoin Multi-Factor Regime Modeling · Evelyn Chen
meta_description: A concise, chart-led summary of Evelyn Chen's Bitcoin multi-factor regime modeling research.
title: Bitcoin Multi-Factor Regime Modeling
subtitle: A multi-signal framework for identifying Bitcoin market regimes and dynamically adjusting exposure.
summary_bullets: Researched 10+ heterogeneous Bitcoin alpha signals spanning valuation, on-chain positioning, miner economics, investor sentiment, and technical momentum.
Developed a multi-signal regime-classification framework to identify low-, intermediate-, and high-valuation market states and dynamically adjust exposure.
Backtested the allocation strategy across multiple market cycles, growing initial capital to 2.82× with 18.6% maximum drawdown, versus 2.68× and 58.4% for Bitcoin buy-and-hold.
Evaluated signal persistence, regime stability, turnover, drawdown behavior, and robustness across parameter specifications.

strategy_rows.rule: Buy when EMA20 / EMA50 − 1 crosses above −5%. Exit at ≥0%, ≤−8%, a 12% price stop, or when leaving the zone.
strategy_rows.rationale: Wait for momentum to recover after deep weakness; exit if the recovery fails.

strategy_rows.rule: Buy when EMA20 / EMA50 − 1 > 4%. Exit below 1% or when leaving the zone.
strategy_rows.rationale: Use a 4% / 1% hysteresis band to confirm the medium-term uptrend and reduce whipsaws.

strategy_rows.rule: Hold BTC only when EMA5 / EMA30 − 1 > 1%; otherwise stay in cash.
strategy_rows.rationale: Stay invested only while short-term momentum remains stronger than the intermediate trend.

strategy_note: Backtest convention: T+1 execution · 0.1% one-way transaction cost · long or cash only.
result_summary: The strategy improved Sharpe from 0.53 to 0.97 and Calmar from 0.52 to 1.75, while reducing maximum drawdown from 58% to 19%.
